_about: Single source of every numeric band and method constant used by the harness,
meaning npm run verify and npm run gen:baseline. Each value carries a source.
'STAGE1.md check N' means the number is copied from the Verification checks table
or its method column. 'Loop A harness choice' means STAGE1.md left the number
unspecified and Loop A fixed it; the reasoning is in PROGRESS.md.
This file is owned by Loop A. Loop B must not edit it. Argue in PROGRESS.md instead.

min_abs_body_yaw_deg.source: Re-specified at the owner's request, argued in PROGRESS.md 2026-08-17. The old floor of 2.0 was recorded by its own source as a 'Loop A harness choice', and PROGRESS.md carries a three line proof that a symmetric QUADX cancels roll-to-yaw coupling EXACTLY, for any per-motor physics: reaching 2.0 deg would need about 44 deg of column asymmetry, and a well tuned quad does not yaw two degrees in a one second roll. What the plant models instead is explicit build tolerance, tangential motor cants of -0.9/+1.4/+0.6/-1.2 deg whose sum against the roll column is -1.1 deg, measured at -0.12 deg of drift over this maneuver. The floor is set where deleting that tolerance model (drift collapses toward 0.00, which is where this check sat for the project's whole life) fails loudly, with margin under the measured -0.12.

expected_sign.source: Loop A provisional choice for a positive (right) roll input with Betaflight props-in rotation. Sign convention: positive r yaws nose left. See PROGRESS.md OPEN QUESTIONS

max_abs_body_yaw_deg.source: The other half of the band, same argument. Coupling scales linearly with the cant table, so 0.60 deg is about five times the modeled build tolerance: someone inflating the invented cants to fake a bigger coupling, which is exactly how the old 2.0 floor would have had to be satisfied, fails this side. The check now guards the tolerance model from both directions instead of demanding a drift no physical quad exhibits.

audio-bed._about: The audio bed has to actually start. A user reported that no music played at all, and nothing in tests/ could have caught it: every audio claim in this project was measured by hand with scripts/audio-probe.js against a graph the probe builds itself, so the shell could stop building its own graph entirely and every check would still pass. These bound the live page instead. The generated sixteenth-note scheduler is gone; the live check now asserts the recorded mp3 is playing.

min_music_gain._about: Music bus gain at the DEFAULT settings, with nothing touched. The run taps a key on the TITLE screen, which is a menu, so what it reads is the menu bed: level 0.5 times MENU_BUS 0.20 is 0.10. The flight bed is level 0.5 times MUSIC_BUS 0.60, so 0.30. 0.05 is a wide floor under the quieter of the two that still catches a silent or unattached bed. The value has not moved; the arithmetic behind it has, because the menu bed did not exist when it was written.

min_music_advance_s._about: Seconds of HTMLAudioElement currentTime that must elapse across a 2.5 s window after the file has started. The generated sixteenth-note scheduler is gone; a stalled or never-started media element stays at 0. 1.0 is a wide floor, not a tempo claim.

max_nodes._about: Web Audio nodes in the live graph. The budget is 64, so this catches an unbounded voice pool without arguing about the exact count. The 59 recorded here before is older than the graph it described: a live run driven the same way this check drives one reads 42 on the title screen, and one of those 42 is the swap gain the music bus gained for the crossfade between the flight and menu crates, so it was 41. The budget is what is asserted, not the count.

craft_body_m.source: The airframe's own published body length, 0.155 m front to back, measured off the drawn BoxGeometry. A 5 mm band because the number is authored, not sampled.

craft_sweep_m.source: Motor at 0.110 m from centre plus 0.0635 m of blade is 0.1735 m. The band spans a 200 to 250 mm class machine, which is what a 5 inch quad is.

craft_radius_tolerance_m.source: CRAFT_R must BE the swept disc, not approximate it: both are now derived from the same two numbers, so any gap at all is a regression. Half a millimetre is floating point slack.

world_scale.source: The world is modelled at 1 times the aircraft's own scale (src/render/frame.js WORLD_SCALE), so a metre in the physics is a metre in the world. It was 1.25 for one round, to answer a report that the drone read too large against the gate and the town. That was the wrong lever: dividing the craft's displacement cannot change the angle a gate subtends, so it made no gate any bigger and it made every course a quarter longer to fly, which is a quarter added to every lap time on the board. Apparent size belongs to the camera and was fixed there, in CAMERA_FOVS. The check divides this back out before banding the airframe, so it is the declared ratio the page has to agree with, not a tolerance.

gate_scale.source: The declared departure from the rulebook, src/game/track.js GATE_SCALE. Here so that changing how big a gate is has to be done in two places on purpose, rather than in one place by accident.

swiss2_modules_min.source: Choosing the Swiss valley with the Alps already built fetches swiss2.js and the files under src/maps/swiss2/ it imports, 49 by its static import closure on 2026-09-28 (the Alps modules it builds through are already there). A floor rather than an equality because the browser may serve some from cache within one page life; anything near this number means the graph really arrived. It replaced the city's floor of 55 when the city was retired, and it is the same property: a world's modules arrive when it is chosen and not before.
